prior.source: 300 self-play games by the FROZEN conv_value_boxA (experience/traj/chess_v0.jsonl)
prior.used_by_the_trainer: 189 -- et8_chess_prior.train SKIPS draws, which carry no outcome signal

beta_rule_as_ruled: compute the L1 curve at beta in {0.5,1,2,4}; run at the SMALLEST beta whose mean L1 shift >= 0.10 (a tenth of prior mass moved); record curve and chosen beta BEFORE the sweep; if no beta <= 4 reaches 0.10, stop and report the table as too flat to test.
why: 0.5 is the smallest of the four whose mean L1 clears 0.10, at 0.1126. The rule selects it, not me -- and it is NOT the beta = 1.0 the design named first. Recorded here before any pairing is played so the choice cannot be read back from the result.
what_the_curve_replaced: on the two-game smoke prior the same curve read 0.012 / 0.024 / 0.048 / 0.099 -- NO beta <= 4 would have cleared 0.10, and by 理's rule that prior was untestable. The 300-game table moves nine times as much prior mass at the same beta. The check was worth running: a prior that is present but inert produces a null that reads as a finding.
bounds: The L1 shift says the prior CHANGES the search's proposal distribution. It says nothing about whether the change is an improvement -- that is what the five pairings measure.
120 positions reached by random legal play from the opening, so the distribution is not the distribution MCTS actually visits. It is a probe of reach, not of importance.
Self-play against the same evaluator: the prior was trained on games this same frozen net played, so the arms are not independent of the training signal.
